questions.q: 3-Hydroxybutanal is warmed with dilute NaOH. The product and the mechanism of water loss are:
questions.explain: Base removes the acidic α-H to give an enolate, which then expels OH⁻; the new C=C is conjugated with the C=O, giving crotonaldehyde.

questions.q: The intermediate formed in an E1cB elimination is a:
questions.explain: In E1cB the proton leaves first, so the conjugate base (a carbanion, an enolate for carbonyl compounds) forms before the leaving group departs; E1 is the carbocation route.

questions.q: Which combination most strongly favours the E1cB pathway?
options: A good leaving group (Br) and no electron-withdrawing group
A tertiary substrate, a protic solvent and no base
A poor leaving group (OH or F), a C=O, NO₂ or CN next to the C–H, and a base
A good leaving group (OTs) and a strong bulky base
questions.explain: An EWG makes the β-H acidic and stabilises the carbanion, while a poor leaving group stops E1 or E2 from competing. Good leaving groups usually react by E2.

questions.q: CF₃–CHCl₂ is treated with OH⁻. The carbanion CF₃–CCl₂⁻ forms and then expels a halide. Which statement is correct?
options: F⁻ is expelled, because it is the only halogen on the carbon β to the carbanion
Cl⁻ is expelled, because chloride is the better leaving group
Cl⁻ is expelled, because the C–Cl bond is the weakest
No halide leaves; the carbanion is simply reprotonated
questions.explain: The chlorines sit on the carbanion carbon itself, so only an F on the β-carbon can leave, giving CF₂=CCl₂. This product could not form by concerted E2, which is evidence for the carbanion.
